How Missing Data Shape the Clinical Picture of Chronic Kidney Disease

Source: original UCI CSV, one-based record 43. rbc = red blood cells.

RenalLens · Missing-data sensitivity

Three rules, different denominators

The explanatory fields define eligibility. The diagnosis label never fills a missing value.

Observed measurements

Use recorded values for each question.
Hemoglobin n = 348, creatinine n = 383, renal pairs n = 380.

Complete cases

Require all 24 explanatory fields to be present.
158 of 400 records remain. We also test a core-five eligibility rule.

Median + mode fill

Fill numerical gaps with global medians and categorical gaps with modes.
All 400 records remain. Filled cells retain their provenance.

Sources: diagnostics.csv, renal_correlations.csv, eligibility_rules.csv. Core five: hemoglobin, creatinine, blood urea, glucose, blood pressure.

RenalLens · Missing-data sensitivity

Eligibility changes the retained cohort

Both rules use observed values. Only the required fields change.

+142

records remain when eligibility uses the five measurements.

CKD retention rises from 17.2% to 66.0%.

Record 43 enters the core-five cohort because all five measurements are present.

Source: eligibility_rules.csv. All 24 includes rbc. Core five includes hemo, sc, bu, bgr and bp. Each bar starts with the same 400 records.

RenalLens · Missing-data sensitivity

The creatinine shift reverses within CKD

The overall median and the median within CKD move in opposite directions.

The all-24 cohort changes who contributes to the summary.

Among observed creatinine values, 62.1% come from CKD records.

After all-24 selection, that share is 27.2%. The retained CKD records have higher creatinine.

Sources: median_shifts.csv, mixture_standardization.csv. Observed creatinine denominators differ from the full-cohort diagnosis counts.

RenalLens · Missing-data sensitivity

Median filling creates a visible concentration

Hemoglobin ECDFs show where the replacement values accumulate.

52 / 400

hemoglobin values take the same replacement value, 12.65.

That creates a 13.0% jump in the filled ECDF.

The extra mass comes from the filling rule. The observed values stay unchanged.

Sources: measurement_values.csv, diagnostics.csv. ECDF = empirical cumulative distribution. Hemoglobin units follow UCI's gms label.

RenalLens · Missing-data sensitivity

Pearson rises while rank correlation falls

The same renal pair tells a different story under all-24 selection.

CKD and non-CKD mix changes. Within CKD, Pearson is 0.543 then 0.846. Within non-CKD, it is -0.101 then -0.117.
Extreme-value sensitivity: omitting observed record 22 changes Pearson from 0.586 to 0.674.

Sources: measurement_values.csv, renal_correlations.csv, diagnostics_renal_influence.csv. Raw axes retain every measured extreme.

RenalLens · Missing-data sensitivity

Scaling changes the first principal component

PCA uses the same 400 filled records and five measurements in both views.

Raw PC1 mainly follows glucose. Standardization gives creatinine and blood urea more weight, with hemoglobin in the opposite direction.

Sources: pca_loadings.csv (eigenvector_weight), pca_variance.csv. Signs follow the published orientation. An entire PCA axis can reverse sign.

Back to record 43

Glucose 204 mg/dL is observed. Only rbc is missing.
The all-24 rule excludes this record. The core-five rule retains it.

Eligibility selects people. The retained cohort changes the overall clinical summary.

Filling changes distributions. The hemoglobin ECDF exposes the repeated median.

Statistics and scale change the picture. Pearson, ranks and PCA emphasize different structure.
